measured_by: CI=true npm run test:ci (the instrument CI uses), full suite, 0 failures, read from .vitest-summary.json within the same second as the run per this file's own stale-artifact warning. RAISED by the area-restricted nav work.
_what_this_is: A FLOOR, not an equality. A run that executes fewer files or tests than this has not tested what this number says it tests. Growth passes and prints a reminder to raise these. Removing tests on purpose means lowering these IN THE SAME DIFF -- the number may only move in a reviewed commit, never by drift.
_why_it_exists: 2026-10-07, run cap6_10 of a worker-cap experiment: vitest printed 'Test Files 338 passed (338)' while six files never ran, because [vitest-pool-runner] timed out starting their workers. The denominator fell from 344 and the summary line still read complete. vitest cannot catch this alone -- the six were never counted, so its own collected total was already 338. Only a number written down earlier can disagree.
_files_is: len(summary.testResults) -- NOT numTotalTestSuites, which counts describe blocks (a 2-file subset reported 4).
_the_arithmetic_of_this_change: +1 file, +18 tests, counted PER FILE from a fresh summary rather than inferred from a delta, because two offsetting errors also add up. New file: src/services/navigation-area-restriction.test.ts, 11 tests (the payroll-limited nav compared as a SET, its unlimited-user mirror, the null-vs-[] distinction, untagged-is-denied). Plus 7 added to the existing src/components/root-redirect.test.tsx, 8 -> 15. 11 + 7 = 18. 387 -> 388 files; 5565 -> 5583 tests. No tests were removed.
_the_lesson: A FLOOR THAT ONLY MOVES DOWNWARD IN REVIEWED COMMITS STILL DRIFTS UPWARD BY NEGLECT, and the drift hides the size of a later removal. Raise this in the commit that adds tests, not 'when convenient': had the floor been 5417, CI would have reported the deletion as -36 and the number would have matched the file.
_raised_in_the_same_commit: ⚠️ RAISED IN THE COMMIT THAT ADDED THE TESTS, which is the lesson the entry below records rather than a new policy. Earlier the same day the floor was 5 behind because growth only prints a reminder, and that drift made a later deletion report -31 when the file carried -36. The reminder is not a to-do; it is this edit.
_the_stale_artifact_finding: ⚠️ THE RATCHET READ A DAY-OLD FILE AND REPORTED GREEN. `test:assert-size` takes `.vitest-summary.json` as an argument and never checks that it describes the run you just did. Measured 2026-11-03: `npx vitest run` reported 384 files / 5494 tests, then `npm run test:assert-size` read a summary stamped Nov 2 14:06 and printed 'ran 379 files / 5385 tests; baseline 379 / 5385' — a perfect match, against yesterday. Only `test:ci` writes the file, and nothing couples the two scripts. In CI they run in sequence so the artifact is always fresh; run by hand, in either order, the ratchet can confirm a run that never happened. That is the same shape this file exists to catch, one layer out: a number written down earlier is worthless if the instrument reads a different run's output. ALWAYS run `CI=true npm run test:ci` immediately before `test:assert-size`, and check the file's mtime if there is any doubt. Reported rather than fixed — making the script refuse a stale summary needs a run id both halves agree on, which is its own change.
_found_by_a_peer_not_by_the_gate: ⚠️ CI PASSED ON THE STALE FLOOR, AND THAT IS THE DESIGN RATHER THAN A BUG: a floor passes on growth and prints a reminder. So the guard degrades silently and the only thing that catches it is a person reading. Had this stayed 12 behind, a later deletion of 30 tests would have reported -18 and read as a smaller removal than it was. Two sessions are editing this file today; whoever lands second must RE-MEASURE rather than add their own delta to the other's number, or the floor ends up below the truth by exactly the amount the first session added.
_why_the_parent_is_recorded:
⚠️ A CORRECT MEASUREMENT GOES STALE WHEN SOMEONE ELSE'S TESTS LAND FIRST, AND THE STALENESS PASSES. Two sessions measured this file today against the same parent c1ff17d8 and got different right answers: 5553 (payroll, +5 wizardOutcome) and 5560 (capture, +12 push 2). Neither is correct for the combined tree, which measures 5565 — VERIFIED BY MY OWN RUN, not taken on the other session's word: git worktrees share one object database, so their unpushed commit was already readable here, and cherry-picking it onto this branch in a throwaway worktree measured 386 / 5565 / 0 failures. Cost 70 seconds and no network. It had been the one figure in this file sourced to a session rather than to a run. Whichever lands SECOND is behind by the other's delta — 12 or 5 — and a floor that is too LOW passes, because the ratchet only checks shrinkage. Not drift by neglect, which _the_lesson already covers: drift by two correct measurements against different parents.

THE RULE: whoever lands second re-measures AFTER rebasing. If this field does not name the actual parent of the commit that last touched this file, the number has not been re-measured and is not evidence.

WHY NAMING THE PARENT IS ENOUGH: the second commit's parent is the FIRST COMMIT, not the shared ancestor both sessions branched from. So the second lander's field names a commit that is not its parent, and the mismatch is visible. Credit to the capture session for the mechanism.

⚠️ IT STILL NEEDS A READER. The removal-style fix is a CI step comparing this field to the real parent, which would make noticing unnecessary rather than required. Recorded, not built — it is a change to the enforcement script rather than to the number, and nobody has ruled on it.
_three_runs_not_one:
⚠️ MEASURED THREE TIMES, AND THE FIRST RUN HAD A FAILURE THAT IS NOT MINE. Run 1: 387 / 5565 / 1 failed - BindingPicker.test.tsx 'preserves field_path when switching between views of the same entity type', the THIRD and last bare query site in that file, which its own quarantine comment says is 'still bare and untested'. Runs 2 and 3: 387 / 5565 / 0 failed. A baseline run with my changes STASHED also failed 1 - but a DIFFERENT test, DocumentsTab.test.tsx 'Save fires documentBlocksService.update immediately'. So the failure MOVES between runs and fires on a clean tree, which is the full-suite-worker-load bare-query race CLAUDE.md §11 names by file and by site. Roughly 1 in 3 full runs on this machine. It is not caused by this change and it is not fixed by it.

⚠️ I DID NOT QUARANTINE THE BINDINGPICKER SITE, deliberately. The file carries a standing ruling against waitFor patches - the magnitude experiment was falsified at 5006 ms against a 5000 ms timeout, and a timeout reports just past its own limit by construction, so no timeout figure can ever evidence slowness. And quarantining the site that happened to lose THIS run would not address the class: the baseline lost a different site. Two of that file's seven tests are already skipped; a third would leave its primary claim and both halves of its secondary claim untested, to buy one green run out of three. The owed work is the named investigation - whether the click on the trigger is PROCESSED at all under load, aria-expanded reaching true - which closes all three sites at once. Reported, not patched.
_why_the_counts_are_trustworthy_despite_: The race changes WHICH test fails, never how many exist. All three runs reported 387 files / 5565 tests. A floor is a claim about the denominator, and the denominator was identical across a failing run and two clean ones.
_the_eight_that_went_red_first: ⚠️ MY FIRST VERSION REDDENED EIGHT EXISTING TESTS AND THE FIX WENT IN THE CODE, NOT IN THEM. Teaching RootRedirect the area landing made it call the THROWING usePresetTheme(), which coupled a component that previously needed only useAuth to the whole theme provider — so root-redirect.test.tsx failed in eight places. The tempting read is 'the tests need a provider mock'. The honest read is that the coupling was real: the component became unrenderable wherever that provider is absent. Fixed by adding usePresetThemeOptional(), mirroring the useFocusOptional / useParkOptional / useEdgePanelOptional convention already in the repo, after which all EIGHT PASS UNMODIFIED — which is the standard for a refactor: if a test breaks, the default is that behaviour changed, not that the test is wrong. The 7 added on top cover the new branch, including the positive wiring (with a nav available, a payroll-limited user lands on /payroll) rather than only the helper that computes it.
